title: Children's prayers
tomorrow: Chicago's group chats are forming. who will Amira sit with?

lines: I DIDN'T WANT TO RUSH HIM.
cards: A toddler in a living room waits until a grown-up goes down into prostration, forehead on the floor, and then climbs on like it's a jungle gym. Now what? It happened to the Prophet ﷺ.
In a report in Sunan an-Nasa'i, he stays down in one prostration so long that the people praying behind him wonder if something has happened.
Afterward he explains: my son was riding on my back, and I didn't want to rush him.

teach.b: It was his grandson, in fact, and he called him my son.
Another report, in Sahih al-Bukhari, has him leading prayer while carrying his granddaughter Umamah: he set her down to prostrate, and picked her up again when he stood.
In these reports children aren't kept away from prayer. They're on its back and in its arms. Praying together isn't a lecture about prayer; it's prayer with a small person in it.
The Qur'an gives words for the other half, praying for them, from Abraham. In Pickthall's words: "My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also)."

teach.h: A WEEK, A HOUSE FILLING UP.
teach.b: Now the week, quickly. A trench, and a leader carrying earth: generous at work. A man told to sleep: the body's right.
Birds that leave the nest: provision is written. A sandal mended: mercy at home.
A door down the hall: the middle door. A psalm and a single soul: keep the tie. Six days, a house filling up, and today a child on a back and a grown-up who waits.

how: Muslim families pray together at home with children standing beside them, and children come along to the masjid; a parent may pray with a little one nearby, and parents ask God for their children in their own prayers.

o: a children's service held apart from adults
praying with children, and for them
the short prayers children learn at school

games.q: who's who in the reports — tap the pairs.
p: rode on his back in prostration
i didn't want to rush him

s: in the reports, children were kept away from the Prophet's prayers
he carried Umamah while praying and waited for his grandson on his back.
the Prophet once stayed in prostration so a child could finish riding on his back
he said afterward: I didn't want to rush him.
Abraham's prayer in the Qur'an asks for prayer to go on in his children
14:40: and some of my posterity also.

games.q: your aunt wants her kids to stay home from the masjid until they can sit perfectly still, so they don't spoil anyone's prayer. what do the reports suggest?
o: she's right; children belong at prayer only once they're quiet.
bring them; the Prophet prayed with children in his arms and on his back.
bring them and let them run; prayer manners don't apply to kids.
games.why: he carried Umamah through a prayer and stayed down for his grandson. the reports put children inside prayer, not outside the door.

practice: Bring to mind the person who first taught you a word worth keeping, a prayer, a blessing, a thank-you. Say that word aloud, slowly, the way a child learns it, one sound at a time.
Then sit with whoever taught it to you in mind, and whoever you might teach it to next.

wordCard.voice: Children's prayers: praying with children, and for them. The Prophet stayed down so a child could finish his ride.

orig.note: Arabic: prostration, forehead to the ground; the moment the grandson climbed on.

carryVoice: Last line of the week: pray together, with a child on your back if need be. Four of ten, and a full week.

sources.ref: Sunan an-Nasa'i 1141 (Shaddad ibn al-Had: a long prostration; 'my son was riding on me and I did not want to hurry him')
Sahih al-Bukhari 516 (he prayed carrying Umamah bint Zaynab, setting her down to prostrate and lifting her when he stood)

sources.q: My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also)
